subject: Post-call: Genomexa offline deployment qualification — operational questions & site map
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Ellen Shaw <ellen.shaw@genomexa.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Genomexa offline deployment qualification — operational questions & site map

Thanks again for your time today, Ellen — good discussion. Summary and immediate next steps below so we have a single checklist to work off for the Private (air-gapped) deployment path. I copied Ben (solutions) and Priyom (field ops) for technical/ops follow-ups.

Quick recap (high level)
- Goal: run Redwood Inference in a fully isolated Genomexa environment (no outbound egress) with on-site inference appliance + private control plane connectivity via one-way data exchange when allowed.
- Key constraints: strict patch windows, SOC2 evidence required, limited physical access to the rack (security escort required), on-site spares must be minimized.

Open items we agreed to action (please reply inline or provide docs where noted):
1) Hardware baseline: please confirm target node count and preferred GPU class (A100, H100, etc.) and whether NVMe hot-spares are allowed on-site. See attachment: site-diagram.png (annotated rack layout).
2) Maintenance window cadence: what recurring maintenance window(s) do you have for non-production systems? We need preferred blackout windows for firmware/OS updates.
3) Upgrade path & rollback: describe current on-site policy for offline OS/firmware upgrades and whether you require staged verification on a standby host.
4) Offline operations & KV cache persistence: do you have an internal policy regarding on-disk caching and tape/air-gapped backups for model state?
5) Service access model: confirm whether we should plan for KMS/HSM integrations or if keys must be managed exclusively by Genomexa (we can support both). See security-reqs.xlsx for items we typically ask.
6) Physical inventory: please populate the attached physical-inventory-template.csv with serials and network port mapping for the target rack(s).

Proposed immediate next steps (ours):
- Ben: provide a short hardware/firmware MOP (2 business days) based on the answers above.
- Priyom: draft an offline upgrade playbook and hit the key rollback controls (3 business days).
- Jonas: consolidate answers and propose 2x time slots for a short on-site readiness call (30 min) next week.

Attachments: site-diagram.png; security-reqs.xlsx; physical-inventory-template.csv (blank copy)

If you can get the inventory and network diagram back to us by Friday EOD PT, we can have a preliminary MOP and playbook ready for review on Monday.

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0172

From: Dr. Ellen Shaw <ellen.shaw@genomexa.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: IT Ops <it-ops@genomexa.com>, Markus Vogel <markus.vogel@genomexa.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Genomexa offline deployment qualification — operational questions & site map

Jonas — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers inline below and I attached our latest network topology PDF.

On the items you listed:
1) Hardware baseline: we are currently planning a 2-node cluster for the first phase; preferred GPU is H100 but we can consider A100 if power/cooling is constrained. NVMe spares: preferred to have 1 hot-spare per rack but approval may take a week.
2) Maintenance window cadence: primary blackout Wed 22:00–02:00 local time (UTC-7) and monthly second Tues 01:00–03:00 for critical patching. Non-critical patches are scheduled quarterly.
3) Upgrade path & rollback: our on-site policy requires staged updates: one passive node validation followed by rolling updates. Full rollback must be tested on a maintenance replica; we cannot accept irreversible changes without snapshot/backup.
4) Offline ops & KV cache persistence: we do allow encrypted on-disk caches; long-term backups must be exported to removable media under sec-escort.
5) Service access model: keys must remain within our KMS; we do not permit external HSMs to hold live keys. We can provide wrapped keys for specific workflows.
6) Physical inventory: attaching network-topology.pdf for networking ports — will populate the CSV and return by Friday EOD.

Two quick asks from us:
- Can you confirm an estimated maintenance MOP duration for firmware updates on the H100 (per node)?
- Do you support air-gapped metrics export that can be pulled manually by our Ops team?

Attachments: network-topology.pdf

Best,
Ellen
Dr. Ellen Shaw
Head of IT Operations, Genomexa Therapeutics
ellen.shaw@genomexa.com | +1 (510) 555-2290

Subject: RE: Post-call: Genomexa offline deployment qualification — operational questions & site map

Ellen — thanks for the fast response and the topology doc, that helps. A few technical clarifications and a short MOP estimate below.

MOP/maintenance estimates (rough):
- H100 firmware + driver update per node (non-disruptive if staged): 45–75 minutes to update and validate on the passive node; rolling update for 2 nodes ~2.5–3 hours including smoke tests.
- If you prefer A100 we estimate ~30–60 minutes per node for firmware/driver validation.

Recommended baseline for Phase 1 (minimum viable on-prem cluster):
- 2x inference nodes, each: 1x H100 (if power & cooling allow) or 2x A100 80GB as fallback; 512GB RAM; dual 10/25Gbps NICs; 2x NVMe devices (1 active + 1 hot-spare recommended).
- On-site spares: 1 NVMe spare + 1 power supply module per rack preferred.

Offline operations notes: we support encrypted on-disk KV caches and provide a validated export/import utility for manual metrics/trace pulls that can be executed by your ops team (no outbound egress required). We will provide runbook steps for manual metrics export (CSV + tarball) in the playbook.

I'm attaching the physical-inventory-template.csv (blank) to simplify the serial/port capture. Please fill main serials, NIC mapping, and PDU outlet assignments.

Next actions (short):
- Ellen: CSV populated + any power/cooling constraints by Friday EOD PT.
- Ben: produce a one-page maintenance MOP and a checklist for staged firmware upgrades (I will deliver Monday morning).
- Priyom: will follow up about secure transport of removable media for backups.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | +1 (650) 555-0188

- Monday 2027-04-26 15:00–15:30 PT
